timing.label: Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: How do you know Devin will respect our no-schema-change rule?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: Why pay for an agent to write a plan a senior engineer writes in ten minutes?

problem.quote: a new engineer needs a week to run it and someone reset that shared database on day two

approach.quote: I will use Devin's environment setup with a blueprint and a root AGENTS.md

evidence.quote: brings up the storefront in under fifteen minutes on a recording

next_step.quote: open one PR with AGENTS.md, the reset script and a proposed blueprint in docs

must_mention.point: Both brands run on a single shared codebase and database
must_mention.evidence_quote: Kadé runs two brands, Lumen Home and Trailhead Supply, on one shared codebase and one shared Postgres database

must_mention.point: The cost of the chosen problem stated in orders, money or engineer-days
must_mention.evidence_quote: roughly five engineer-days per hire plus one outage

must_mention.point: One Devin capability for the first session with one reason it beats an alternative
must_mention.evidence_quote: environment setup with a blueprint and a root AGENTS.md, because that is the only capability that removes the shared-database risk without touching a migration

must_mention.point: The proof of success described as an observable artefact rather than a command
must_mention.evidence_quote: a fresh session, following only the instructions, brings up the storefront in under fifteen minutes on a recording

must_mention.point: One thing the plan refuses to do because of the schema freeze, main or budget
must_mention.evidence_quote: on a throwaway branch, never on main

article_plural_slips: "zero touches of the shared database" — "touch" is uncountable here; "no contact with"
sentences_to_rerecord: Ask: I need thirty minutes of the on-call engineer's time

accuracy.anchor: All five points named with a quotable sentence; cost given as engineer-days plus one outage (anchor: 27–30 = every point, one with a number).

structure.anchor: Problem, approach, evidence, next step each present and in order; update kept Outcome → Evidence → Risk → Next action → Ask (anchor: 22–25 = all four present, order held).

customer_relevance.anchor: Four numbers from the brief (two brands, a week, 400 orders, 3% drift) and the Lamp Week deadline absorbed in one line (anchor: 16–18 = numbers from the brief, one assumption flagged).

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: All five segments on target within ±5 s; one filler in 6.6 minutes; no tag questions (anchor: 11–13 = every segment on, fillers under 1/min).

recovery.anchor: Both objections followed acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer; the "how many orders" interruption was answered with one number and the skeleton resumed (anchor: 7–8 = pattern held under interruption).

stems: "The risk I am carrying is… and here is how I bound it…" — say the risk before the customer asks.
"Specifically, you would see…" — turn every claim into one observable.
"That is fair. The boundary is…" — keep the acknowledge → boundary pair under ten seconds.
previous_run_comparison: First recorded run for dryrun on lab 00; no previous run to compare with.
